title_kr: 원불교 교육이념을 기반으로 한 원광유아교육의 방향 제안
abstract_kr: The objective of this study is to propose directions of Wonkwang early childhood education connected with contents of Nuri Curriculum, curriculum of national level, by finding out ideals, purposes, precepts, and contents of Wonkwang early childhood education. First, it is necessary to establish the systems of WonKwang early childhood education on the basis of Won-Buddhism’s ideals of education. It is also important to find out how the operating guidelines of Wonkwang early childhood education reflects periodical changes and various social needs because it has not been revised yet since its publication in 1996. And it is needed to be modified and complemented up to date, like describing something suitable for early childhood education. Second, it is necessary to operate the contents of Wonkwang early childhood education in connection with the contents of 5 areas in Nuri Curriculum. Finally, it is necessary to find out activity methods about the contents of Wonkwang early childhood education such as Cultivating the Spirit, Inquiry into Human Affairs and Universal Principles and Choice in Action suitable for early childhood development.The study is meaningful in leading Wonkwang early childhood education based on Won Buddhism’s ideals of education to ensure internal stability in general and universal ways in connection with Nuri Curriculum.

title_kr: 원불교 청년세대의 취업, 결혼, 출산 의식 실태
abstract_kr: The purpose of this study is to investigate employment, marriage and childbirth status and perception of the young generation of Won-Buddhism, reflect on the direction of low birth rate measures that can be attempted at a religious level, and provide basic data for establishing low birth rate measures from a long-term perspective. To this end, the demographic sociological characteristics of the young generation of Won-Buddhism, preparation for employment, job search experience, and awareness of marriage and childbirth were surveyed. The survey was conducted on 514 young adults aged 20 to 39 years old through the Internet online survey. As a result, 28.6% of young people in Won-Buddhism were single-person households, and the ratio of single-person households was higher than that of ordinary young people in Korea (15%). Second, the youth generation of Won-Buddhism was found to be more heterogeneous than age (students vs. graduates, employed vs. unemployed, job seekers vs. workers, full-time vs. non-regular workers, workers vs. self-employed). Third, the most difficult thing for the young generation of Won-Buddhism in their job search was I dont know what I want and do well (20.8%). Fourth, the young generation of Won-Buddhism had 62.6% of the willingness to give birth, and the willingness to give birth (75%) was lower than that of ordinary young people in Korea. Based on these results, First, the development of customized policies in response to multi-differentiation of the youth generation. Second, development and operation of career exploration programs for young people with immature careers. Third, development of healing programs for deficient and long-term NEET and fourthly, expand education to restore family values in the denomination.

title_kr: 지구를 모시는 종교 - 동학과 원불교의 ‘천지론’을 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: This paper tries to interpret Donghak and Won Buddhism as ‘Earth-serving Religions’ through the globalogical implications contained in Heaven and Earth Cosmology of Donghak and Won Buddhism. Donghak asserted the idea of ‘Heaven and Earth parents(天地父母),’ and Won Buddhism preached the doctrine of Grace of Heaven and Earth(天地恩), which considers Heaven and Earth as parents and teachers, and serves them as gracious beings. Two doctrines - Heaven and Earth Parents and Grace of Heaven and Earth – have its roots in ancient East Asian Heaven and Earth Cosmology. This shows that Won Buddhism is an East Asian Buddhism which combines East Asian cosmology with Buddhism. In addition, Donghak and Won Buddhism can be characterized as “Earth religions” in that they recognize Earth as a community and recommend to serve it. Lastly, the doctrine of Grace of Heaven and Earth(天地恩) and Ethics of Three-fold Unity(三同倫理) in Won Buddhism have a globalogical significance in the age of Earth at risk in that they go beyond conventional anthropocentric ethics.

title_kr: 대학생 생활명상 프로그램 개발 및 효과 측정 - ‘중심(中)’ 개념을 활용한 몸·마음·관계 연구 -
abstract_kr: This study is a quasi-experimental design before and after the nonequivalence control group to develop Living Meditation program for university students and to test the effects of bad postural habits, state-trait anxiety and Korean multidimensional assessment of interoceptive awareness (K-MAIA) Methods. In the introduction, the necessity of Living Meditation program for college students was explained in consideration of modern social phenomena, and the theoretical framework and concept of ‘Jung (中)’ of one’s body, mind and relationship were defined. The hypothesis of ‘There will be differences in the K-MAIA between the experimental group with 12-session Living Meditation program and the controlled group (hyperthesis 3)’ was accepted: The K-MAIA score of the experimental group was 3.17±.84 points before the experiment and 3.44±.60 point after 12-session Living Meditation program(t=-2.05, p <.049), and the K-MAIAscore of the control group was 3.30±.49 point and 3.45±.76 point respectively(t=-1.26, p <.217). However, bad postural habits (hyperthesis 1), state-trait anxiety inventory (hyperthesis 2) appeared to be statistically insignificant and were rejected. As a conclusion and suggestion, we ultimately seek a way for college students to simply apply meditation in their lives for the sake of mindful practice based on Living Meditation program. In addition, this study is expected to be utilized as basic data for the systematic development of the Living Meditation manuals between lecturers and learners and for the domestic and overseas application and diffusion of the Living Meditation program.
keywords_en: Korean multidimensional assessment of interoceptive awareness (K-MAIA)

title_kr: 자비명상의 실천체계 탐색 - 「자애의 경」을 중심으로-
abstract_kr: Recently, various meditation methods such as mindfulness meditation, intensive meditation, and insight meditation derived from Buddhist practices are gaining popularity not only, but are also used in the field of psychological counseling. Meditation techniques created based on Buddhist meditation have succeeded in establishing itself as a meditation industry as the market size of several trillion won has grown globally. However, from the standpoint of Buddhism and Buddhism Psychology, the indiscriminate use of meditation practices in various fields without knowing which theories and practices of Buddhism are derived can damage the original purpose of Buddhism and distort the original purpose of meditation. There is a risk to it.This research analyzes the major scriptures related to self-compassion meditation and studies the characteristics and challenges of modern self-compassion meditation through examples of programs related to self-compassion meditation. Traditional way of meditation, based on early sutras, has few points that limits it to be practiced by the mass. On the other hand, programs from the Western world, that utilizes less technological approach, focuses on enhancing resilience. This research concludes that self-compassion meditation, being used as a tool to only be used for overcoming inner suffering that one is currently facing, has limitations. In order to expect sustainable improvements, changing the focus of program to practicing of the benefiting oneself and others is suggested.

title_kr: 영남지역 범패 연구의 현황 검토와 연구 양상

On the other hand, although Busan Yeongsanjae was designated as a cultural property the fastest in the Yeongnam region, the number of independent studies was smaller than in the Masan region. The reason is that, under the leadership of the Conservation Society and the academic society, an academic conference has never been held, and public events and transmission activities and publicity were relatively low. This is because, under the leadership of the Conservation Society and the academic society, an academic conference has never been held, and public events and transmission activities and publicity were relatively low. On the other hand, the full-fledged period of research on Beompae in Busan started in 2007, which coincides with the time when the album production of <Youngnam Beompae> and Guams sound source became known to the academia. This suggests that it is very important to secure image and sound data in the study of scoundrels. In addition, since the beompae takes place at the site of the Buddhist ritual, various aspects may appear depending on the situation. In this regard, field studies are essential.

title_kr: 세계문화유산 ‘산사, 한국의 산지 승원’의 세계유산적 가치 탐색
abstract_kr: In 2018, the UNESCO 42nd World Heritage Committee listed 7 temples in Tongdosa, Boseoksa, Bongjeongsa, Beopjusa, Magogsa, Sunamsa and Daeheungsa as World Heritage Sites. The name of the list is ‘Sansa, Buddhist Mountain Monasteries in Korea’, and Korea has become a world heritage holder with 14 ‘Korean Seowon’ listed in 2019. Although it is only 1.25% of the worlds heritage, it is expected to expand further through further efforts. Since a cultural heritage has to go through numerous routes until it is listed as a World Heritage, and development strategies such as improving errors are established in the process, its own efforts should continue regardless of whether it is listed or not. Especially, when it is selected as a World Heritage Site, it is promoted not only to Shenyang of nationality but also to the status of local governments with the heritage. Therefore, the meaning of the World Heritage should be evaluated in the national sense beyond the cultural context.Until the ‘Sansa, Buddhist Mountain Monasteries in Korea’ becomes a World Heritage Site, it must meet one or more of the ten criteria required for the World Heritage List: Among them, OUV(Outstanding Universal Value) should be proved as the top priority, and in addition, authenticity and integrity should be provided, and sustainable management and protection requirements should be met. This study examined how cultural values as a World Heritage were met.

title_kr: 지구위험시대, 유가생태수양론의 再考 - 왕양명의 만물일체설과 치양지를 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: This study aims to suggest ‘how should the relationship between humans and nature be established, and what are the responsibilities and roles of humans’ as a fundamental question to solve the era of global risk, to examine the Confucian ecological philosophical value of Wang Yangmings ‘all thing as one body’ Theory, and to illuminate the meaning of ecological cultivation of Zhiliangzhi(致良知) as a moral cultivation for completing ‘all thing as one body.’Confucian philosophy tells that human beings have total responsibility as a manager of nature rather than individual responsibility as a member of nature, and to fully take charge of this, the necessity of moral discipline is emphasized above all else. Wong Yangming originally regards the essence of the mind as one body, and he ontologically believes that humans and all things exist in an organic relationship like one body in which Yichi(一氣) circulates, but due to selfishness, an individual desire, they are in a state of being seperated from all things in the universe. Therefore, he asserts that human can become truly oneness with all things in the universe by eliminating seflish desires through the acquired moral cultivation called Zhiliangzhi and by recovering and completing Liangzhi, which is the subject of spiritually intelligent correspondence with all things in the universe.As described above, ‘All things is one body’ theory and Zhiliangzhi seek a transition from human-centeredness to human-orientedness through fundamental reflection on the innate status and role of humans in the relationship between humans and all things in the universe in the era of ecological risk. In addition, they have a characteristic that they presents the paths of internal self-fulfillment as well as external solution of ecological problems.

title_kr: 두 사건에서 보는 지구적 전환(two geological turn): 우리는 어떤 지구를 상상할 것인가 -홍대용의 자전설과 자법어물(資法於物), 라투르의 대지설과 사고 전시
abstract_kr: Historically, every change in Earths position in space has led to a revolution in the socio-political order. This article examines two thinkers who revolutionized the socio-political order of all things by reestablishing the relationship between the earth and the beings on earth. They are Hong Dae-Yong(1731-1783), a philosopher in the late 18th century of the late Joseon Dynasty, and Bruno Latour(1947-), a French philosopher and political ecologist. Based on the astronomy theory Hong developed the revolutionary theory expressing the equality of all things that emphasize human beings and things are all one when viewed from heaven. In his Uisanmundap, he quotes the words of The sage learns from all things, and suggests the point of view of learning from things’. Non-humans are not only the background of human beings but also move with their own activities and this point of view preempts the ontological theory of equality seen from todays new materialistic perspective. This can be seen as an embryonic concept of the Donghak ideas of Gyeongmul(敬物) in the future. On the other hand, Bruno Latour, who took the lead in interdisciplinary research of science and society in the 21st century with the Actor-Network-Theory(ANT) between humans and non-humans, propose us to shift the perspective of the earth from globe to terrestrial and from geo to gaia that he suggests can be a new solution for mankind, who is lost in the era of the Anthropocene. Although the two thinkers global perspective shift occurred with a time difference of 250 years (a quarter of a millennium), the thought is the same in that they insist on the socio-political innovation that a shift in perspective on the planet we live in can cause. The comparison of these two thinkers’ theories gives us insight into what kind of earth we can imagine.
keywords_en: ’The Sage Learns from All Things(資法於物)’

title_kr: 형벌과 박해 사이 -초기 한국천주교회의 순교 개념 재고-
abstract_kr: The early history of the Roman Catholic Church in Korea is characterized by a series of persecutions and martyrdoms. In Christian religious narratives, a history of persecution is often transformed into tales of martyrdom. However if historical narratives focus primarily on stories of martyrdom, they risk distorting important historical details as well as oversimplifying competing viewpoints and claims. This article considers whether the penalties and punishments, viz. decapitation, hanging and posthumous dismemberment were arbitrarily inflicted upon Roman Catholics by the Joseon government. On the whole, the legal basis for the punishment of Roman Catholics in Joseon was well-established in Joseon legal codes, but the absence of or confusion surrounding the concept of religion caused problems. I suggest that the Roman Catholic Church countered its illegalization by employing the language of martyrdom. In fact, the act of dying for a religious commitment was a very strange phenomenon in the Joseon society. In Joseon, martyrdom was incomprehensible without the modern concept of religion. Therefore, to understand martyrdom meant to acknowledge and accept the modern concept of religion. We can suppose that martyrdom anticipated and facilitated the adoption of the modern concept of religion.

title_kr: 자연 현상과 農占 문화의 사례 고찰 -한국 세시풍속을 중심으로-
abstract_kr: Nature and humans cannot be separated from each other. The ancient thinking system that adapted itself to nature has been greatly changed by humans’ wrong greed for dominating nature. As a result, all sorts of natural disasters have occurred, which is threatening the survival of all the animals and plants. Thus, it is urgently needed to have the ancestors’ wisdom that observed and applied natural phenomena to their daily living. This study revealed that the farming divination culture shown in Korean traditional seasonal customs was the experiential fruit of closely observing natural phenomena, by examining some cases of farming divination and natural phenomena in limited several areas.As a prediction of good and bad harvest, the farming divination is largely one of the elements of divination culture. Especially, the core heart of farming is to be well-harmonized with the energy of heaven, earth, and human, so divining the good and bad harvest of the year through farming divination must be a basic attitude for making human’s life affluent. The farming divination includes the experiential farming divination through natural phenomena such as moon, star, wind, and weather, and the farming divination judging through animals/plants, insects, animal sounds, grains, and fruits. They are all shown in traditional seasonal customs, and also handed down by observation and experiences for a long time. Therefore, it is no exaggeration to say that it could be regarded as one of the experiential sciences without using scientific equipments.

title_kr: 현대 일본의 ‘생명영성’과 ‘치유영성’ -동일본대지진과 코로나19사태를 중심으로-
abstract_kr: This article considers the spirituality that emerged from the natural disasters of Japan in the 21st century. In 1995, Aum Shinrikyo sarin attack on the subway and a series of crimes were reported, and the overall impression of ‘religion’ in Japanese society deteriorated. Furthermore, many existing religions are facing a decrease in the number of believers due to factors such as the declining birthrate and aging population. On the other hand, ‘seishinsekai(精神世界: mean spiritual world; as New Age movement)’ or ‘spiritualism’, which are separated from existing religions, are accepted in various forms.2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and the Tsunami and Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster accident that occurred in the 21st century on March 11, 2011, and the COVID-19 disaster that occurred in 2020 (and is still in progress at the time of writing the paper), and other disasters have created a new interest in spirituality. In this paper, we will deal with ghosts (testimony) in the disaster area, the nuclear power plant shrine, the Great Buddha of Corona, and the Amabie boom as examples.

title_kr: 이동녕의 대한민국임시정부 수립과 유지·옹호 활동
abstract_kr: Lee, Dong-nyeong(李東寧) played an important role in establishing the Korean Provisional Government. He served as the first chairman of the Korean Provisional Congress(大韓民國 臨時議政院) of the Korean Provisinal government to determine the organization and political system of the government. Also The government reorganized the government organization according to realistic situations for stable state administration. He played his responsibility and role as a government minister. He served as acting prime minister and interior minister to minimize the governments administrative vacuum. Furthermore, as the Korean Provisional Government faced difficulties in managing state affairs due to internal and external conflicts and confrontations, it struggled to deal with the chaotic government.In order to maintain and defend the the Korean Provisional Government, decided on future routes and made efforts to realize them. In 1921, he was deeply concerned ways to the unification and union of the independence movement group, and as a result, he recognized that the problems of the independence movement group were conflict and division. As a solution to this, he insisted on the integration and unity of the independence movement group centered on the Korean Provisional Government, to realize this, he returned to politics in 1924 and implemented a number of policies. In 1926, he led the formation of a government’s cabinet as chairman of the Korean Provisional Congress. Lee, Dong-nyeong formed the Korean Independence Party(韓國獨立黨) and the Korean National Party(韓國國民黨) in In 1930 and 1935, Based on this, it played a major role in establishing a power base to maintain and defend the Korean Provisional Government while implementing modern party politics.He promoted the integration of the independence movement group with the Korean Provisional Government at the center. After participating in the establishment of the Korean Provisional Government, Lee, Dongnyeong continued to strive for unity, solidarity, and integration of independence movement organizations. His efforts and will laid the foundation for the formation of a unified parliament and a coalition Government of the right and left wing in the 1940s.
keywords_en: the Korean Provisional Congress(大韓民國臨時議政院)

title_kr: <해제> 민족 언론《 동아일보》게재 불법연구회 기사
『글로벌화시대의 일·한 신종교: 묘지회교단과 원불교』의 구조와 성격
신자유주의의 무한경쟁과 코로나 팬더믹 위기를 사회적 경제와 공공성으로 돌파한다 -김흥주 편저, 『사회적 경제와 공공성』(도서출판 신정, 2021)을 읽고-
원불교 법인정신과 ‘佛法에 대한 선언’
abstract_kr: Is Won-Buddhism Buddhism or National Religion? There has been considerable discussion within Won-Buddhism on this question, and the researchers who stuck to the view that Won-Buddhism is national religion tried to emphasize Won-Buddhisms identity as national religion through a literature critical attempt on Songkyus 「the foundation history of Buddha research institute」.In particular, the omitted aspect of national consciousness or nationalistic colors in「 the foundation history of Buddha research institute」 or excessive Buddhist-oriented technology has been interpreted as an inevitable situation caused by the suppression of pseudo religion by Japan.In this regard, it analyzed the reason why 「the foundation history of Buddha research institute」 had to show its Buddhist identity focusing on the context of the narrative.It was identified that the world would be drawn and realized by ideal world and Buddhism(佛法) that pursued by Sotaesan, through the process of the fact that it pursued the right truth by excluding falsehood(虛僞) and sorcery(邪術) from the process of seeking truth of Sotaesan, the fact that it pursued the right truth by excluding falsehood(虛僞) and sorcery(邪術) from the process of seeking truth of Sotaesan, absolutely perfect new Buddhist ceremony(會上) by the nomination on Buddhism, that is, to build a new Buddhist idea after Daegak, and the Declaration of Buddha Dharma(佛法) after Dialect(坊堰) work and prayers for Dharma authentication(法認祈禱).In other words, it showed that the meaning of establishing the new Buddhism ceremony based on Sotaesans Buddhism is to lay the foundation for the new religion toward the salvation of mankind and the people by having foundation of the new eras moral civilization on Buddhism, not just for an expediential alternative to avoid Japanese oppression.
keywords_en: the foundation history of Buddha research institute

title_kr: 원산 서대원의 생애와 사상 재조명
abstract_kr: Wonsan Sŏ Daewon was an early disciple of Master Sot’aesan who organized the principles and ideas of Master Sot’aesan. Sŏ Daewon served as a research director, auditor, vice-principal of the General Headquarter, and a member of the Head Circle Council in the Buddhadharma Research Society. As such, he was trusted by Master Sot’aesan and played a significant role in further developing the Buddhadharma Research Society. Nevertheless, the interest of Won-Buddhist Order and academia in Sŏ Daewon are not high, and the evaluation of him is also divided. Therefore, this study aims to shed new light on Sŏ Daewons life and thoughts, triggering academic interest in him.First, Sŏ Daewon lived a life in which he devoted his true belief to truth, doctrine, teacher, and order. And he wholeheartedly sought to the way. He wrote high-quality articles and lectures in various fields. Second, Seo Daewons representative writings, “Dharma instruction and the Origin of Il-Won-Sang,” summarized Sotaesans doctrine, which is clearly different from that of traditional Buddhism, as the key word Il-Won and Three Great Principles. This article was a pioneering achievement. After liberation, this article was expanded and developed into a Won-Buddhist order by Soongsan Park Giljin, the first paper on Il-Won truth in the Won-Buddhism academic world. In this work, some of Park Gil-jins research reveals much of the same reasons and their relevance as Seo Dae-wons writings.
keywords_en: Dharma Instruction and the Origin of Il-Won-Sang

title_kr: 원불교 교강 선포의 근 · 현대 종교사적 의미 -불교적 관점을 중심으로-
abstract_kr: ‘Doctrine’ means ‘the teaching of creed’ and refers to the case that Sotaesan Park Jung-Bin declared fourfold grace · four essentials as an important path of life and three creeds · eight articles as an important path of study’ at Bongnaejeongsa Temple in Byeonsan, Buan, in April 1920. Sotaesan went through ‘the declaration of Buddhist truth’ and ‘the planning of Ilwonsang’ before the proclamation of the doctrine. The core of the Sotaesans doctrine was a concrete way to implement Buddhas teaching in real life as shown by those processes and the name of ‘Buddhist research association’ at the time.The Buddhist world of 1920s was the period when the various informations on Buddhist doctrines were distributed in various ways, in accordance with various published books and magazines on Buddhist history and thought, etc. Particularly centered around the religious world, information on the flow of social change as well as Buddhism was spread throughout the country from the March First Independence Movement. Under these circumstances, there was a trend of Buddhist reform. Baek Yong-sung, Kwon Sang-ro, and Han Yong-un, etc. were the leading figures of the trend. Sotaesan was self-aware of this movement of reform Buddhism and founded ‘Buddhist research association’ after the proclamation of the doctrine.Sotaesan was particularly influenced by the encounter with Hakmyeong, the representative monk of Baekyangsa Temple. In terms of doctrine, Seon and discipline, he was the most prominent monk among the family members of the Baekyangsa Temple after monk Baekpa. Hakmyeong was a revered monk representing his time in the fields of doctrine, Seon, discipline, and literature. He was a great Seon master who shared Seon riddle with some revered Chinese and Japanese monks.The modern · contemporary meaning of religious history on the proclamation of ‘the doctrine’ is that ‘reform Buddhism, which advocates per iodization · habituation · popularization has emerged on this land’. Sotaesan made clear his ambition and identity to create Buddhist world by saying, ‘It is the morality of Buddha that we learn, and it is the morality of Buddha that we teach younger generations’.
keywords_en: an anniversary certified by the truth
a prayer for the certification by the truth
blood stamps on a white paper

title_kr: 원불교 2만 교화단장 양성 정책의 교화성장 효과 분석 - 다층성장모형 적용 -
abstract_kr: This study analyzes the effects of the Won -Buddhist training policy for 20,000 edification unit leaders, which was conducted across the whole order from Wonki 95 (2010) to Wonki 97 (2012), on the increase in the number of edification unit leaders and the number of Dharma service attendants by applying a multilevel growth modeling. The analyses showed that the effects of increasing the number of Dharma service attendants and the number of edification unit leaders were significant. The effect of increasing the number of Dharma service attendants remained significant even after the policy was discontinued, but the effect size was ‘small.’ On the other hand, the effect of increasing the number of edification unit leaders showed a ‘medium’ level of effect size, but most of the effects were short-term during the implementation period of the policy program. In addition, it was tested whether the increase in the number of Dharma service attendants by the policy program was mediated by the increase in the number of edification unit leaders. The mediating effect was also verified, but the effect size was not high. In regard to the reason that the mediating effect was not high, the effect of the change in the number of edification unit leaders on the number of Dharma service attendants was found to be notably low considering the ideology of edification through edification units, in which one leader edifies nine members. Based on the analysis results, policy implications and future research direction to promote edification through edification units were presented.

title_kr: 자이나교의 성적 금욕론(2) -브라흐마차리야 서약-
abstract_kr: Jainism proposed five vratas by adding brahmacarya vrata (vow of chastity) from the four yamas that existed in the Śramaṇa tradition. Analyzing the usage examples of various literature in Jaina Lakṣanāvalī, the meaning of “brahmacarya” is 1) conduct based on a pure soul(jīva ), 2) abandonment of desire, 3) control of sexual desire and cessation of sexual activity. This meaning is an extension of the existing concept of brahmacarya by transforming it into an idea of Jainism.The mendicant great vows in Chapters 2-3 of Yogaśāstra are summed up by 18 prohibitions of sexual contact and the five types of violations. However, according to the Tattvārthasūtra commentaries, the violation is defined as simply maithuna, whose meaning extends from sexual intercourse to sexual activity in general. On the other hand, the theory of sexual abstinence of layperson consists of a double guideline. That is satisfaction with wife and complete avoidance of other women, requiring more detailed caution and violations.Finally, the Jain theory of non-violence also applies to sexual asceticism. Because sexual intercourse kills microorganisms in the sexual organs, it should be prohibited. In this strict abstinence tradition, the concept of veda(sexual desire), a pioneering idea of sexuality peculiar to Jaina, was presented.

title_kr: 중국 초기선종의 성립에 관한 일고찰 - 우두선(牛頭禪) 사상을 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: This paper is about the thought of Zen(禪) in Fǎ róng(法融, 594657) and the sect of Niu-tou(牛頭宗). The purpose of this study is to explain delicate the Niu-tou Zen(牛頭禪) which had taken a brilliant role in Zen Buddhism in China of bygone days. The Order of Zen Buddhism insists on the faith that Buddha and Human beings have originally the same in true nature. Furthermore, Geonsung(見性) isn’t the discourse of the true nature, but manifests oneself it. According to the 1st Bodhidharma’s coming from India, China Buddhism has turned over a new leaf and became more pratical religion than just dogmatic concentration of the teachings of Buddha. He put Lankāvatāra-sūtra(『楞伽經』) on a essential text of Zen Buddhism and practised a ‘meditation staying focused on wall’(凝住壁觀) as a method of the practice on his Zen. As time passed, his tradition of Zen’s practice was divided into two kinds of South and North in China. Namely, one is ‘Mindlessness’(無心) of Southern Zen and the other is ‘Escape of thouhgt’(離念) of Northern Zen. A fully separate sect from previous sects was the Order of Niu-tou which had established by the 1st zen master named Fǎ róng. He was based on the doctrine of the Sānlùn school(三論宗) in China, avocated ‘None of action zen’(無事禪) and ‘Extinction of all Vipassanā’(絶觀) as a practice of Zen throughout Prajña-Śūnyatā(般若空觀) of Mahāyāna Buddhism. The 4th master (法持) succeeding a brilliant thought on Zen by Fǎ róng actually established the Sect of Niu-tou as a independent sect in China Buddhism. They were called as an ‘Independent from Extinction of Emotion Sect’(泯絶無奇宗), a ‘Prajña-śūnyatā Sect’(般若空宗), or a ‘3rd Zen Sect separate from north-south two zen sects’ tradition’ by the 5th Zōng mì(圭峰宗密, 781-841) in the Huá yán zōng(華嚴宗) in China. The thought of conformability of the meditative(禪) and doctrinal aprroaches(敎) have given the background on it of the 4th Chéng guān(清涼澄觀, 737-838) and the 5th Zōng mì in the Huá y án zōng. However, the sect of Niu-tou had gone away into a page of history in China Zen Buddhism before China’s Song(宋) Dynasty, casting in their fortunes with a decline of the Sānlùn school in late Tang(唐) Dynasty. So, to conclude, the aim of this essay is to expose the true reason of the ‘jiàn xìng chéng fó’(見性成佛) on Zen Buddhism by investigating thoroughly the Niu-tou Zen which had presented a most powerful thought in Zen Buddhism in China.

title_kr: 儒 · 佛의 修養 · 修行의 윤리적 의미에 대한 비교분석 -知訥과 朱熹를 中心으로-
abstract_kr: In the ethics of East Asian philosophy, Xiu-Yang[修養] or Xiu-Xing[修行] of Confucianism and Buddhism is a methodology of self-completion and a representative methodology for cultivating ethical human beings. In Eastern philosophy, the two philosophies had a profound influence on each other for thousands of years. However, the theoretical logic and ultimate goal of Xiu-Yang[修養] or Xiu-Xing[修行] of these two philosophies are still different. Therefore, in this thesis, we have looked into the oriental philosophy, focusing on Ji-Nul[知訥] and Zhu-Xi[朱熹], which had a profound influence on the philosophy of Confucianism and Buddhism in Korea.In the two philosophies Xiu-Yang[修養] or Xiu-Xing[修行], the premise is that all human beings have universal ethical possibilities. Both philosophies considered that human ethical possibilities could be realized through Xiu-Yang[修養] or Xiu-Xing[修行]. However, the methodology and theoretical for realizing the ethical standards they argue, namely, Xing-Li[性理] of Zhu-Xi[朱熹], Kong-Ji-Ling-Zhi[空寂靈知] of Ji-Nul[知訥]. The explanation was different. Ji-Nul [知訥] asserts that Ding-Hui-Xiu-Xing[定慧修行] and Kan-Hua-Chan[看話禪] should be practiced on the premise of a vow of great mercy. Kong-Ji-Ling-Zhi[空寂靈知] or Wu-Xin[無心] is said to be an ethical standard. Wisdom based on these ethical standards is realized through ethical conduct. There is no temporal or semantic gap between wisdom and action. In addition, the ethical behavior caused by Kong-Ji-Ling-Zhi [空寂靈知] is unconsciously close to intuitive judgment. On the other hand, Zhu-Xi[朱熹] emphasizes the subjectivity of Xin[心], and this Xin[心] maintains a state of psychological tension as Jing[敬] in the process of all Xiu-Yang[修養]. Zhu-Xi [朱熹], in order to conduct ethical judgment and conduct, first restrained his human desire with Ju-Jing-Han-Yang [居敬涵養]. In addition, it emphasizes the need to realize Xing-Li[性理] through Ge-Wu-Zhi-Zhi[格物致知]. Afterwards, you must observe yourself and maintain Zhong-Jie[中節] before all words and actions by knowing based on discipline. Therefore, it can be said that Zhu-Xi[朱熹]s ethical human perfection is step-by-step and based on rationalistic judgment.

title_kr: 일심삼관을 통한 원묘요세의 정토사상 고찰
abstract_kr: This study explores the relationship between the Buddhist practice of Wonmyo Yose (圓妙了世, 1163-1243) and the White Lotus Society he founded. Yose explored the concept that “the one mind has true thusness of all existence” from the three viewpoints of: emptiness, nominal designation, and the mean. He clarified that these three viewpoints are the one mind, and the one mind is the three viewpoints. Yose’s “three viewpoints in the one mind” starts from the understanding that whatever has arisen as the result of causes and conditions is characterized by emptiness and nominal designation, and occupies a midway position between two extremes. Yose revealed the truth of emptiness by teaching the dharma that says “all dharmas produced through dependent arising are empty” based on his own understanding of “the three viewpoints in the one mind.” The latter is a teaching of Tiantai, who eagerly studied texts by Nāgârjuna such as Zhonglun [Mūla-madhyamakakārikā] and Dazhidu lun [Treatise on the Mahāprajñāpāramitā]. When Yose recited the Miaozong chao, a sub-commentary on Sutra of the Meditation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, he said that a doubt he had on one passage was resolved: “Attain Buddhahood with this mind. This mind is Buddha.” To summarize his understanding, the words “attain Buddhahood” from the passage is divided into “Response Buddha” and “Fruition Buddha.” “Response Buddha” is one of the Buddhas of other quarters that has a distinct form; “Fruition Buddha” refers to the “Amitabha Buddha within oneself” which is inherent in the mind of sentient beings. Yose then clarified his understanding with the three contemplations of Tiantai. He embraced Yongming Yanshou’s teaching of Nianfo Chan (念佛禪), which combines reciting the Buddhas’ names and Chan meditation based on the belief that “the mind is the Pure Land.” Based on one of the tenets of the White Lotus Society (“three viewpoints in the one mind”), Yose propagated the ritual of repentance based on the Lotus Sutra. Based on the practice of seeking to be reborn in the Pure Land, Yose understood that all dharmas, including the principle of cause and effect that rules all people and sages, arise according to causes and conditions, and he practiced seeking enlightenment and saving sentient beings at the same time. This study should provide more incentive for others to explore Yose’s philosophical stance on “the three viewpoints in the one mind,” and to explore his thoughts on the Pure Land that are reflected in his practice of the dharma flower samadhi and the White Lotus Society.
keywords_en: Three Viewpoints in the One Mind

title_kr: 《달마도》의 형식적 특징과 도상 해석 - ‘벽관(壁觀)’의 구현과 의미를 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: In this paper, I would like to clarify what points of appreciation for the painting under the theme of Bodhi-Dharma(《Dalmado》) are based on the teaching method of Bodhi-Dharma. First of all, it examines the formal characteristics of the representative works, and examines its iconographic meaning by linking it with the relevant authority (典據).To describe the point first, the core characteristic of Bodhi-Dharma painting is the eye of the wall or state of the wall(壁觀 Byeokgwan) . Why was such an iconographical feature mentioned, and explained the key term byeokgwan in 『Bodhi-Dharma’s Four Act theory(菩提達磨四行論 Borridalmasahaengron)』, which is said to be Bodhi-Dharmas kinship. In conclusion, the theory of Bodhi-Dharmas theory of engagement(理入 yiyip) and four deed(四行 sahaeng), as well as ‘seeing Buddha (見佛 gyeonbul) or truly seeing’, is conclusively discussed how it is connected to ‘the state of the wall’.And how these characteristics were reflected in 《Dalmado》, first of all, we analyzed the formal characteristics in detail through 〈Dalmado〉 masterpiece by Kim Myung-guk representing Korea of Joseon period. Next, we selected 〈Dalmado〉 in the Song Dynasty(owned by the National Palace Museum in Taiwan) and 〈Dalmado〉 in the Muromachi period in Japan, and compared the traditions and characteristics in the context of East Asia in Korea, China, and Japan.Lastly, based on the definition of ‘seeing Buddha’, which is conveyed by Bodhi-Dharma, the importance of ‘engagement and speculation’ emphasized in the existing academia is also important, but the importance of ‘engagement and seeing Buddha’ was emphasized. In conclusion, the meaning of 《Dalmado》 as its realization was discussed with the eye of the wall or state of the wall. as a term that implies this core teaching of Bodhi-Dharma.
keywords_en: Byeokgwan(壁觀 state of the wall)

title_kr: 春秋時代 天命觀의 變化와 命運天 觀念의 生成에 관한 硏究 - 道德天과 命運天의 비교를 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: In ancient Chinese philosophy, the discussion of ‘Tian-Ming(天命)’ has been developed in various ways throughout the times. In particular, the greatest characteristic of the idea of Zhou(周)’s ruler during the period of the replacement Yin(殷) by Zhou(周) was ‘Virtue(德)’, and it was presented as the only condition that only the virtuous king could receive ‘Tian-Ming(天命)’. As the West-Zhou(西周) became debilitated, the ‘Tian-Ming(天命)’ was lost day by day, and the spirit of resentment · regret · abuse of Heaven(天) came to emerge. This fundamental doubt naturally led to the change of the Viewpoint of Tian-Ming(天命觀), and the secular meaning of ‘Ming-Yun(命運)’ was added to ‘Tian-Ming(天命)’ concept.In ‘Tian-Ming(天命)’ theory of Confucius(孔子), the contents of the ‘Dao-De-Tian(道德天)’ and ‘Ming-Yun-Tian(命運天)’ are intrinsically embedded, and it emphasizes ‘Knowledge of Tian-Ming(知命)’. Confucius, on the one hand, accept the need to inherit ‘This culture(斯文)’ as Tian-Ming(天命), and on the other hand, a man accept what he could not do like as ‘Life and Death(生死)’.In particular, the academic meaning of the creation of the idea of Ming-Yun(命運) is as follows. First, ‘Dao-De-Tian(道德天)’ is a government-level politics, while ‘Ming-Yun-Tian(命運天)’ is a human life science related to the individuals luck. Second, it provides theoretical clues that distinguish between Politics Confucianism(政治儒學) and Moral nature Confucianism(心性儒學). Third, the concept of ‘Ming-Yun(命運) promote the development of rational rationalism determined by morality, and at the same time promote the development of celestial determinism, such as the knowledge of Tian-Ming(天命) through the change of heaven. Fourth, the objects of Tian-Ming(天命) were moved ‘from emperor to people · from nation to individual, and the contents were regulated in categories such as ‘life and death · riches and honors’ which greatly influenced the formation of later Tian-Ming(天命) theories.

title_kr: 우익지욱의 『논어점정(論語點睛)』에 보이는 경전주석 방식의 특징
abstract_kr: The high priest Ouyizhixu(蕅益智旭, 1599-1655) in the era of Ming(明) and Qing(淸) Dynasty of China, was a great monk and a excellent researcher who represented the Buddhist world in China. He had conducted extensive writing activities Based on the ideology that all of the Buddhist Dharma result in nianfosanmei(念佛三昧) and he was a first Buddhist monk to comment on the Confucian scripture Lunyu(論語). He wrote the commentary book Lunyudianjing(論語點睛) in 1647. The Lunyudianjing is an important work in Classics history of Ancient China as well, because it contains ideological fragments of Mengzizeru(孟子擇乳), the book of the high priest Ouyizhixu(蕅益智旭), who had already been practiced. In this thesis, the characteristics of the scriptural commentary method used by the high priest Ouyizhixu(蕅益智旭) in order to solve the main text of Lunyu were broadly classified into four types and reviewed. The characteristics of the four scripture commentary methods are as follows. First, Confucian scriptures and Buddhist jing(經) · lu(律) · lun(論) San Zang(三藏) and the high priest Ouyizhixu(蕅益智旭)s writings were cited. Second, including wangyangming(王陽明, 1472-1528)s writings Instructions For Practical Living And Other Neo-Confucian Writing(傳習錄), radical Yangming scholar Li Zhi(李贄, 1527-1602)s Evaluating the Four Books(四書評) and zhuzibaijiashu(諸子百家書) were cited. Third, the high priest Ouyizhixu(蕅益智旭) severely criticized Zhu Xi(朱熹)s Commentary on the annalects of Confucius(論語集注). Fourth, the commentary was not limited to the interpretation of the main text of Lunyu, but the commentary itself was used as the public security of Buddhism. The high priest Ouyizhixu(蕅益智旭) tried to find the point of contact between the enlightenment of Buddhism and the Confucian mind through these four scriptural commentary methods.

title_kr: 진경시대 <금강전도>의 회화사적 의의 - 유불도 삼교사상을 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: The culture of an era had created the new shape through the process of consilience with a race’s own culture and a foreign culture. In this treatise, I’d like to investigate the meaning of pictorial history in the era of true-view landscape painting that had pursued the harmony in changes, by clarifying the world view in the aspect of Neo-Confucianism of Zhouyi(周易) and the influential relation with Taoism and Buddhism appeared in 〈Complete View of Geumgangsan Mountain〉(金剛全圖) by Gyeomjae Jeong Seon (謙齋 鄭敾).In the latter period of Joseon, the painting style of Jeolpa (浙派畫風) declined, the true-view landscape painting based on the style of the true-view landscape painting and on Chinese painting style of the Southern School (南宗畫風) achieved the great results in the aspect of pictorial history. Especially 〈Complete View of Geumgangsan Mountain〉 had the thought of five natural elements of Yin and Yang (陰陽五行思想) and the reason of abstruseness (玄妙之道) on the basis of Taoim and Buddhism. And also, that picture held the three thoughts ; Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism, as a painting of Taoism in the middle stage of connecting 〈Mongyudowondo〉(夢遊桃源圖) in the early Joseon with the picture 〈Scene of the Banquet around the Yoji Pond〉(瑤池宴圖) in the later Joseon.Neo-Confucianism influenced variously on the many fields in the later Joseon when the culture of true-view landscape painting was blooming. Among them 〈Inwangjesaekdo〉(仁王霽色圖) by Jeong Seon had the friendship between Jeong Seon was a master of the true-view landscape paintings and Yi, Byeong-yeon was a great poet of the true-view landscape poems, and that picture showed us the visible thought of Yin and Yang. In addition, he expressed the cosmology with Big Three ; body, shape and use as the central figure in 〈Complete View of Geumgangsan Mountain〉, in which Mountain Geumgang was regarded as the utopia by Koreans.To conclude, in 〈Complete View of Geumgangsan Mountain〉 he expressed the spirit of harmony and balance in changes that appeared in the three thoughts ; Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism as the meaning of history of thought and picture in the era of the true-view landscape painting.
keywords_en: the Era of True-View Landscape Painting

title_kr: 댄스만달라 프로그램의 심리 치유적 효과 - 스트레스 대처방식, 사회적 지지에 미치는 효과를 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: This study is a quasi-experimental study that introduces DANCEmandala academically and analyzes its psychological healing effects through social science experiments. In the introduction, we introduced Areeradh K Tri-siddha the creator of DANCEmandala, and defined the concept of DANCEmandala to help you understand the basics of dance mandala. In the text, the theoretical background of the DANCEmandala, the four layers of consciousness, the five koshas, and the eight degrees of the Four Truths, were explained in connection with the dance mandala. In addition, the structure was described based on the overview of the Dance Mandala Program, the DANCEmandala 7 Spirals and the DANCEmandala Map. And the DANCEmandala program was operated as a single group pre-post design to measure the effects of stress coping methods and social support. As a result, the stress coping method was statistically significant, and the DANCEmandala program showed a positive effect on the stress coping method, and the social support was not statistically significant. As a hypothesis, the DANCEmandala program will have an effect on the stress coping method. As a result of testing, the stress coping method of the subjects was statistically significant from 1.75±0.50 points before the DANCEmandala program to 2.08±0.39 points after the program (z = -2.953, p=0.003) increased. As a result of testing, the DANCEmandala program will have an effect on social support. As a result of testing, the social support according to the DANCEmandala program intervention was statistically significant, from 3.70±0.63 points before the program to 3.90±0.42 points after the program (z =-. 926, p=0.178). As a conclusion and suggestion, we intend to provide data for the development of a new movement meditation program using the DANCEmandala program.

법인정신(法認精神)과 ‘교강(敎綱)’ 선포 정신의 계승 -지구의 위기에 직면하여-
abstract_kr: This study shed new light on the meaning that Won-Buddhism proclaimed Gyogang (敎綱) as a solution to cure modern civilization which reached the limit. At this moment, the human race is experiencing enormous suffering due to COVID-19. It can be a tragic made by a flood of human desire. Won-Buddhism was begun to reform the human spirit and make people live coexisting with substances as their true owners. Especially, in 1919, Beobin sacred affair (法認聖事) got certification of Sotaesans religious body from the wold of the truth as he and his students showed the spirit of being able to die without any regrets (死無餘恨). The declaration of the Buddha-dharma and proclamation of Gyogang, the enactment of the basic doctrines, followed by it mean that Won -Buddhism began in earnest as the new religion.Won -Buddhism appeared claiming to advocate the right dharma-assembly (正法會上) in the era of decline of the Buddha-dharma. This is because it inherits Mahayana Buddhisms spirit of Sigisangung (時機相應). That is, it tried to realize the appropriate Buddha-dharma for those days at the peoples level. The proclamation of Gyogang is the important event to try to create modern Mahayana Scripture through the philosophy of Prajna or transcendent wisdom, the core of the idea of the Mahayana. Gyogang is the Buddhadharma modernly restructured as shown in Treatise on the Renovation of Joseon Buddhism (朝鮮佛敎革新論) published in 1935.Won - Buddhism that has inherited Mahayana Buddhism should realize the idea or myth of Bodhisattva modernly. Its because prayers of being able to die without any regrets also claim to advocate the spirit of Mahayana of the modern meaning which aggregates sat-paramita (六波羅蜜). Therefore, Won - Buddhism has something to do with the spirit of folk Buddhism, popular Buddhism, and engaged Buddhism and can be the religious body that actively realizes the Buddha-dharma. The pessimistic future of humankind is predicted to require religious roles. Its because the cross-border and universal idea of humankind functions as the spirit of religions to be able to cope with capitalism. Socialization of the Buddha-dharma argued by Won – Buddhism means to go the way of it.

title_kr: 원불교 마음공부 모델 연구
abstract_kr: The mindful practice of Won Buddhism is based on the truth of Il-Won, that is our true nature. The practices are conducted through the Gateway of Practice based on True Voidness and Marvelous Existence and the Gateway of Faith based on Retribution and Response of Cause and Effect. Moreover, it aims for a paradise world where spiritual civilization and material civilization are well harmonized through the Great Opening of spirit.The two sides of the truth of Il-Won-Sang, which is the basis of Won Buddhisms ideology, are revealed in two aspects according to the discernment of the mind as it is, and the method of mindful practice can be presented in two directions: the practice in rest and the practice in action. All mindful practices can take these two directions as the basic form, which is a model of nature-phenomena.In addition, the truth of Il-Won-Sang can be explained by three attributes: Emptiness, Fullness, and Rightness. Accordingly, it is possible to classify the Gateway of Practice based on True Voidness and Marvelous Existence into threefold Study: Cultivation the Spirit, Inquiry into Human Affairs and Universal Principles, and Choice in Action. It constitutes three aspects of practice. This can be presented as a model of nature-phenomena-action.Furthermore, the role of the Gateway of Faith based on Retribution and Response of Cause and Effect in mindful practice is also essential. This should be considered in the expansion of the basic model of mindful practice and in terms of relationship and environment that are conditions of mindful practice.In other words, in terms of the dynamic side of the mind, or the side of execution, if it is expanded, the influence of the practice must be taken into account, even the relationship with the surrounding human relations such as family and friends, and the social and ecological environment. The result again forms the sensory condition of our mindful practice according to the principle of cause and effect, which also needs to be considered crucial in the model of mindful practice. Thus, a model of nature-phenomena-action-relation is presented as an extension that included the Gateway of Practice and the Gateway of Faith.Through the model of mindful practice, a more systematic and practical application will be possible to better understand and change oneself and the world by understanding, keeping, and using the mind well within daily life conditions.

title_kr: 無學自超의「佛祖宗派之圖」 작성목적과 의미(Ⅱ)
abstract_kr: This paper is to examine what the purpose was that Jacho created 「BuljoJongpajiDo」. For this purpose, Chapter II reviews the writing background and the structure of the 「BuljoJongpajiDo」. The 「BuljoJongpajiDo」 was created and first published shortly after the Jacho became the master of Hoeamsa(檜巖寺) temple. This leads us to realize that the「 BuljoJongpajiDo」 was the work expressing the legitimacy of Jacho as the representative of Naong(懶翁) School.A newly revealed fact is that the sequence of Naongs memorial service became unusual in the process that a plague occurred in Hoeamsa after Jacho become the master of Hoeamsa and Jacho had to leave the temple because of it. It is also clearly mentioned that Jacho’s position in Naong School became weak by the plague and he published again「 BuljoJongpajiDo」 to restore his authority.Then, Chapter Ⅲ shows that the creation intention of Jacho’s 「BuljoJongpajiDo」 was to break the relationship between Naong and Honsu(混脩) and to prove Jacho was the legitimate heir of Naong. In addition, it is revealed that Jigong was excluded from the succession(legal tradition) of his teachers in the recognition of the Jacho. For this problem, a reasonable solution is suggested with “The relationship between Jacho and Jigong” and “The change in perception of China due to exchanges of Yuan-Ming and Goryeo-Joseon.”

title_kr: 중화권과 일본의 21세기 방생의식 - 생태계 보호를 위한 대안적 사례를 중심으로 -
abstract_kr: This paper constitutes a preliminary study on approaches to resolving clashes between environmental protection and Buddhist animal release rituals in East Asian countries that follow Mahayana Buddhism, particularly China and Japan.The ritual of bangsaeng (releasing captive animals) fulfills the doctrine of bulsalsaenggye (the rule against killing animals) and loving compassion for all living things. However, in modern times, animals used for Buddhist animal release rituals are commercially bought and sold, placing the practice in conflict with the goals of environmental preservation. Therefore, those who promote the continued practice of animal release rituals are attempting to expand the scope of the traditional principles of the ritual (such as loving compassion for all living things) and transform the practice to revive its purpose of promoting ecological stability.For example, in Tibet, some Buddhists are seeking to expand the concept of animal release to include plant life. In countries of the East Asian cultural sphere, shelters for animals commonly kept as pets constitute another such example. Other attempts to expand the scope of animal release include Buddhist rituals to guide the spirits of aborted babies to the heavenly realm, or the practice of suyeon (隨緣) animal release to encourage respect for life based on the interrelationship of all living things in everyday life.Moreover, in order to regulate indiscriminate animal release rituals, governments and local administrative bodies have enacted regulations and ordinances. In 2004, the Japanese parliament passed The Act to Prevent the Devastation of the Ecology by Certain Foreign Species. (Law No. 78). In China as well, under the sponsorship of the State Administration of Religious Affairs, a petition concerning animal release rituals was submitted to representatives of Buddhist groups across China on July 30, 2014. In addition, on June 1, 2020, the Beijing Ordinance for the Management and Protection of Wild Animals was passed and promulgated. In the case of China, it can be observed that following China’s emergence as the epicenter of the coronavirus pandemic, regulations concerning the problem of releasing wild animals for ritual purposes have become stricter and public awareness has increased.In conclusion, East Asian countries that follow Mahayana Buddhism have been seeking harmony between animal release rituals and environmental protection goals, attempting a variety of practical alternative approaches that go beyond simply reinterpreting doctrine.
